subject: physiology
title: Digestion and absorption: enzymes, bile and malabsorption

steps.tx: Digestion begins with **ptyalin** salivary amylase on starch and lingual lipase, then gastric pepsin on protein in acid, intrinsic factor for vitamin B12, protective mucus and gastrin stimulation. Pancreatic trypsin activates zymogens, lipase with colipase splits fats, amylase finishes starch, bicarbonate neutralises acid under secretin and cholecystokinin control, and brush border lactase and sucrase with peptide uptake finish absorption. Each site digests a different macronutrient in cascade before the border completes it.
steps.say: The mouth starts starch digestion, the stomach adds acid pepsin for protein and intrinsic factor for vitamin B12, and the pancreas delivers the heavy enzymes once secretin and cholecystokinin call. Trypsin switches on other zymogens, lipase needs colipase for fat, and bicarbonate neutralises acid so enzymes can work. The enzymes table follows each site, and the brush border disaccharidases and peptidases finish the job.

vis.alt: Table of digestive secretions by site with enzymes and substrates: salivary amylase and lingual lipase in the mouth, acid pepsin and intrinsic factor in the stomach, pancreatic trypsin amylase and lipase in the duodenum, brush border disaccharidases and peptidases.
vis.caption: Each site digests a different macronutrient; the brush border completes it.

steps.tx: **Bile** is synthesised in liver, stored in gallbladder, released when cholecystokinin contracts the sac, forming micelles that solubilise fats while ninety five percent recycles through the enterohepatic loop, itching in cholestasis and forming gallstones painful in the right upper quadrant on ultrasound. Fats leave as chylomicrons into lymph against very low density lipoproteins from liver, floating as steatorrhoea when malabsorbed, carrying fat soluble vitamins A, D, E and K whose K failure raises INR and bleeds, while ursodiol dissolves small cholesterol stones in selected patients.
steps.say: Bile acids made in the liver and stored in the gallbladder squeeze into the duodenum under cholecystokinin, wrap fat into micelles, and mostly return from the ileum to the liver, the recycling loop drawn in the figure. Absorbed fat rides chylomicrons through lymph with vitamins A, D, E and K, so malabsorption floats pale stools and can bleed from vitamin K lack. Ileal disease breaks recycling, stones block ducts, and itching betrays cholestasis.

vis.alt: Enterohepatic circulation of bile acids: liver makes bile, gallbladder stores it, cholecystokinin contracts the gallbladder to release it into the duodenum, bile acids form micelles with fat, and about 95 percent is reabsorbed in the terminal ileum and returned to the liver by the portal vein.
vis.caption: Bile acids are recycled: ileal reabsorption returns most of the pool to the liver. Ileal disease causes bile acid malabsorption.

steps.tx: Carbohydrate and protein uptake uses **SGLT** sodium glucose cotransport, GLUT5 for fructose, and PepT for small peptides, while lactose failure breathes hydrogen and sucrase failure waters stools. Malabsorption spans coeliac disease by tissue transglutaminase, chronic pancreatitis by faecal elastase, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth by breath tests, Whipple disease with arthralgia, and abetalipoproteinaemia with acanthocytes, split by osmotic diarrhoea stopping when fasting against secretory diarrhoea continuing, calculated by stool gap, and vitamin B12 marking the terminal ileum.
steps.say: Glucose rides sodium into the enterocyte through SGLT1, fructose enters by GLUT5, and small peptides use PepT1, all powered by the sodium pump in the cell diagram. Lactose intolerance ferments to hydrogen on breath testing, while coeliac disease, pancreatic failure and bacterial overgrowth each malabsorb by a different mechanism. Osmotic diarrhoea stops with fasting, secretory diarrhoea does not, and the terminal ileum remains the sole home for vitamin B12.

vis.alt: Enterocyte schematic: SGLT1 brings glucose and galactose in with sodium, GLUT5 brings fructose in, PepT1 brings small peptides with hydrogen, GLUT2 releases all three sugars at the basolateral side, and the sodium potassium pump powers the sodium gradient.
vis.caption: Glucose and galactose ride sodium (SGLT1); fructose uses GLUT5; all leave by GLUT2; the Na+/K+ ATPase drives it all.

steps.tx: Tests target the failing step: **faecal elastase** for pancreas, hydrogen breath tests for lactose and overgrowth, D-xylose for mucosa, the historic Schilling test for B12, and duodenal biopsy showing villi. Support replaces enzymes as Creon with meals, medium chain triglycerides bypassing lymph, vitamins replaced and a dietitian planning, while total parenteral nutrition rests the gut at refeeding phosphate risk and growth plots falter until tracked. Stool testing therefore guides targeted replacement.
steps.say: Working through the gut in order, faecal elastase is indicting the pancreas, breath hydrogen is indicting lactose or overgrowth, xylose is indicting mucosa, and duodenal biopsy is showing villi directly. Treatment then replaces what is missing, pancreatic enzymes with meals, medium chain fats that bypass lymph, and vitamins under a dietitian plan. Resting the gut with parenteral feeding risks refeeding phosphate falls, and faltering growth plots demand action.
